boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, map-listed destinations along the University Avenue–Downtown Palo Alto corridor just beyond Stanford’s main entrance.

cards.title: Palo Alto Transit Center
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor, Palo Alto
cards.notes: Use this regional mobility hub to orient yourself before continuing along University Avenue toward downtown destinations.
cards.short_summary: A transit connection point beside Stanford.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies the Palo Alto Transit Center as adjacent to Stanford University and served by five transit providers, including Stanford’s Marguerite shuttle.
cards.access_notes: Transit fares and service availability vary by provider; check the operating provider before travel.

cards.title: Palo Alto Southern Pacific Station
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor, 95 University Ave.
cards.notes: Pause outside the Streamline Moderne station building and use the National Park Service history as a prompt for noticing its design.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic station on University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Palo Alto Southern Pacific Station at 95 University Avenue and identifies its architectural and engineering significance.
cards.access_notes: View from the public streets and transit areas; follow posted station rules.

cards.title: Stanford Theatre
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor, 221 University Ave.
cards.notes: Look for the theater’s neon marquee on University Avenue, then check its program page if you want to plan a screening.
cards.short_summary: A downtown film theater with a visible marquee.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Theatre states that it is located at 221 University Avenue in downtown Palo Alto and that its neon marquee is a University Avenue landmark.
cards.access_notes: Screenings require a ticket; consult the theater’s current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Lytton Plaza
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor, 202 University Ave.
cards.notes: Take a short outdoor break at the plaza and look for its fountain, seating, bicycle racks, and public art.
cards.short_summary: A small civic plaza with outdoor features.
cards.evidence_claim: A City parks report locates Lytton Plaza at 202 University Avenue and describes seating, a fountain, bicycle racks, and public art.
cards.source_title: Palo Alto Parks and Recreation Master Plan
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plaza; observe any posted City rules or event restrictions.

cards.title: Downtown Library
cards.subtitle: University Avenue–Downtown corridor, 270 Forest Ave.
cards.notes: Step into the branch for its adult books and media collections; confirm current opening hours before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A public-library stop one block off University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Palo Alto City Library lists Downtown Library at 270 Forest Avenue and says it has books and media collections for adults and children.
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary by day; the official location page posts current hours.

cards.title: Palo Alto City Hall
cards.subtitle: University Avenue–Downtown corridor, 250 Hamilton Ave.
cards.notes: Use the City Hall address as a downtown waypoint, then consult the City’s public information for services or meetings.
cards.short_summary: A civic landmark off University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Palo Alto phone directory lists City Hall at 250 Hamilton Avenue in Palo Alto.
cards.source_title: City of Palo Alto Phone Directory
cards.access_notes: Public access and meeting schedules may vary; review City notices before entering.

cards.title: Heritage Park
cards.subtitle: University Avenue–Downtown corridor, 300 Homer Ave.
cards.notes: Walk the edge of this City park on Homer Avenue as a quiet outdoor detour from the University Avenue commercial blocks.
cards.short_summary: A named City park beside downtown Palo Alto.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s public parks inventory lists Heritage Park at 300 Homer Avenue and gives its size as 2.01 acres.
cards.source_title: City of Palo Alto Public Parks Inventory
cards.access_notes: Outdoor City park; use public paths and follow posted park rules.

cards.title: Museum of American Heritage
cards.subtitle: University Avenue–Downtown corridor, 351 Homer Ave.
cards.notes: Find the museum at Homer Avenue and check its official exhibit and visiting information before planning an indoor stop.
cards.short_summary: A named museum destination beside the downtown corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s parks master plan identifies Williams Park at the Museum of American Heritage, located at 351 Homer Avenue.
cards.source_title: Palo Alto Parks, Trails, Natural Open Space & Recreation Master Plan
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s official website for current exhibit access and any admission terms.

cards.title: Elizabeth F. Gamble Garden
cards.subtitle: University Avenue–Downtown corridor, 1431 Waverley St.
cards.notes: Follow the self-guided tour map through the historic garden and watch posted signs for house or garden-area closures.
cards.short_summary: A public historic garden near downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Gamble Garden says it is at 1431 Waverley Street, is a public garden, and is open to the public for free every day.
cards.access_notes: The garden notes that the house and south garden may close for special events; observe posted signs.

cards.title: Cogswell Plaza
cards.subtitle: University Avenue–Downtown corridor, Lytton Ave. at Bryant St.
cards.notes: Use this small City plaza at Lytton and Bryant as a named landmark while exploring the blocks north of University Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A compact public plaza in the downtown grid.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s parks master plan lists Cogswell Plaza at Lytton Avenue and Bryant Street and identifies it as City-owned.
cards.source_title: Palo Alto Parks, Trails, Natural Open Space & Recreation Master Plan
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space; follow any posted City regulations.
